core.title: Name every plan-declared produce/consume artifact in the code that moves it through Cargo
core.given: A wagon document (a plan artifact under the plan root) declares the wagon's data contract — produce[]: artifacts the wagon owns; consume[]: artifacts it takes from other wagons — and a module in this stack moves Cargo for that wagon
core.when: the wagon's Cargo-moving code or its declared contract is written or changed
core.then: Name every declared produce[].name and consume[].name artifact in the module(s) where that wagon moves Cargo, so declaration and carried data cannot drift apart.
prefer: Use plan-matching named constants for artifact names at the Cargo call sites, so every get/put names exactly what the plan declares.
If the wagon no longer owns an artifact, correct the plan instead.
Name your modules as you like; no particular filename is required — what matters is that the module moving the wagon's Cargo names its artifacts.
avoid: Plan produce/consume lists diverging from what is actually put/got through Cargo.
Putting a wagon's declared names only in a shared or unrelated module that does not move that wagon's Cargo.
Trying to suppress a finding: this rule's findings are not suppressible.
unless: The repository declares no wagon contract at all (not applicable).
The wagon has no implementation anywhere: an unimplemented feature, not a broken contract; another rule governs it.
core.why: The core wagon-contract schema only checks that the contract is well formed; only a per-stack check reading this stack's source and its Cargo idiom can see whether the code carries the declared artifacts.
evidence: For every wagon document under the plan root with an implementation, each produce[].name and consume[].name string appears in at least one Cargo-moving module.
The stack's wagon-contract check reports no findings; the check run (CI) passes — strict, not suppressible.
verification: Read every wagon document found recursively under the plan root (profile: roots.plan); collect produce[].name and consume[].name artifact names; flag any name that no Cargo-moving module names.

The core wagon-contract schema validates the document's shape — both produce and consume lists, each entry carrying an artifact name, and produce entries also a contract and a telemetry URN — wherever the plan lives, but cannot know whether the stack's code puts those artifacts into Cargo: that means reading this stack's source and its Cargo idiom, which only the per-stack check does.

Recognise a wagon implementation structurally — a module that moves artifacts through Cargo, per the profile's Cargo-call source idiom (profile: idiom.source_syntax#cargo_calls) — never by filename; filename-based naming heuristics are exactly the fitted checks to avoid, and consumers may name modules as they like.

Not applicable, deliberately, in two cases: (1) the repository declares no wagon contract — nothing to honour; (2) a contract is declared with no wagon implementation at all — an unimplemented feature, not a broken contract, belonging to whatever rule governs unimplemented plan, since reporting it here would fire on every freshly planned repository. The check judges code that exists against the contract it claims, not the absence of code.
Strict disposition, severity 4: a finding is not suppressible and fails the check run (CI).

Scope of the check: wagon-to-module association is not explicit — it verifies only that at least one Cargo-moving module names each declared artifact, not that the naming module is the one that moves that wagon's Cargo.

fires: A wagon document in the plan root declares a produce[] or consume[] artifact name that no Cargo-moving module names, while an implementation of that wagon exists.
A Cargo-moving module is edited and stops naming an artifact its wagon document still declares.
A wagon document gains a new produce[]/consume[] entry while a wagon implementation already exists, and no Cargo-moving module names the newly declared artifact.
doesNotFire: The repository declares no wagon contract at all.
A wagon is declared in the plan but has no implementation anywhere (unimplemented feature, governed by another rule).
A contract entry is added and the Cargo-moving code already names (or is updated to name) that artifact.
Repositories on other stacks: this core is realized per stack, and a realization fires only on its own stack.
Only the shape of the wagon document is wrong (core wagon-contract schema validation, not this rule).

profileRequirements.meaning: Path of the root of plan artifacts; wagon documents live below it and the check reads every wagon document found recursively under this root.
The plan-artifact kind that declares the wagon data contract (the wagon document).

The stack's source construct by which a module moves artifacts through Cargo — the executable call form the check uses to recognise Cargo-moving modules structurally (never by filename) and to locate where declared artifact names must appear.
profileRequirements.bunValue: cargo.get(name) / cargo.put(name, value) method calls on the Cargo passed to the wagon (e.g. in runWagon(step, cargo): const basket = cargo.get(CONSUMES); cargo.put(PRODUCES, { confirmed: true, basket });)

profileRequirements.meaning: Languages of production source; the realization's language activation fact draws its values from here — necessary but not sufficient to identify the stack, so the language-scoped activation itself stays in the realization.

bunOnly.text: Plan-matching name constants used at the Cargo call sites: `export const CONSUMES = "orders:priced-basket"; // plan: consume[].name` / `export const PRODUCES = "orders:confirmed-order"; // plan: produce[].name`; in `runWagon(step, cargo)`: `const basket = cargo.get(CONSUMES); cargo.put(PRODUCES, { confirmed: true, basket });`.
bunOnly.reason: The worked example is written in this stack's module/export syntax and Cargo call form; bun.json stays the reference example for other stacks.

neutralityNotes: Cargo and the wagon produce/consume data contract are ATDD-core concepts, not stack specifics, so they stay in the neutral core. Three things could not be made neutral and remain Bun-only: (1) the stack-identity activation facts (language typescript/javascript — its values supplied by the profile's tooling.languages, since language alone does not distinguish Bun from Node.js or Deno — and change stack_is_bun) — the neutral core is scoped to a stack by its profile instead; (2) this rule's detector, family and finding ids (bun_interlocking_infrastructure, checks/wagon_contract_honoured.mjs, declared_artifact_not_named_by_cargo_moving_code), which the core's verification describes generically; (3) the concrete fix-hint code snippet and the 'wagon.ts' filename illustration, dropped from the core because bun.json is delivered as the worked reference example. Severity 4 and the strict, non-suppressible disposition are kept in core verification per the notProfileKeys policy. The profile's plan root carries the path itself (plan); the recursive plan/** traversal of wagon documents below that root is core verification behavior, with the Bun activation's path_glob kept as the realization's derived form. Recognising a Cargo-moving module structurally needs the stack's Cargo source-call idiom, stored as idiom.source_syntax#cargo_calls: these are executable source-code method calls used by the check — a source-syntax fact, not a construct of plan artifacts, so idiom.plan_syntax does not cover them. The realization's language activation values come from tooling.languages, while the language fact itself stays Bun-only because language alone does not identify the stack.
